    def format_cursor_data(self, data):
        """
        Return a string representation of *data*.

        .. note::
            This method is intended to be overridden by artist subclasses.
            As an end-user of Matplotlib you'll most likely want to get the
            data displayed in the cursor by using Axes.format_coord.

        The default implementation converts ints and floats and arrays of ints
        and floats into a comma-separated string enclosed in square brackets,
        unless the artist has an associated colorbar, in which case scalar
        values are replaced by their colorbar label.

        Parameters
        ----------
        data : scalar or array-like
            The data to format.

        Returns
        -------
        str
            A string representation of *data*.
        """
        if np.ndim(data) == 0 and isinstance(self, ScalarMappable):
            # Mimic a scalar-array conversion.
            value = data.item()
            if self.norm.vmin == self.norm.vmax:
                # Display the value if the norm is degenerate.
                return f"[{value}]"
            neighbors = self.norm.inverse(
                np.interp(value, [self.norm.vmin, self.norm.vmax],
                          [0, 1]))
            if isinstance(neighbors, np.ma.MaskedArray):
                neighbors = neighbors.filled(np.nan)
            if np.isfinite(neighbors).all():
                if isinstance(self.norm, mpl.colors.LogNorm):
                    neighbors = np.power(10, neighbors)
                return f"[{neighbors[0]:.4g}, {neighbors[1]:.4g}]"
        return f"[{data}]"
